title: Superconducting dome and field-enhanced superconductivity of PLD synthesized Nd1-xEuxNiO2 thin films
authors: Wenlong Yang, Qiang Zhao, Xingke Fu, Gaofei Ren, Zhongjing Wu, Zhen Chen, Jianping Sun, Boseng Wang, Jiacai Nie, Pengtao Yang, Jinguang Cheng
abstract: We report on the synthesis of infinite-layer Nd1-xEuxNiO2 (0<x<0.7) thin films using pulsed laser deposition (PLD) followed by topotactic reduction with CaH2. Resistivity measurements on these films reveal a superconducting dome within the doping range 0.2<x<0.5, which is wider than that achieved by molecular beam epitaxy and comparable to that obtained by chemical synthesis. The x=0.3 PLD film exhibits the optimal superconducting transition temperature Tc~31 K, much higher than those grown by other vacuum epitaxial techniques. This result indicates that PLD is an ideal approach for fabricating high-quality, high-Tc Nd1-xEuxNiO2 superconducting films. Magneto-transport measurements reveal robust field-enhanced and re-entrant superconductivity in both underdoped and overdoped regimes. At low temperatures just above the onset Tc, the Hall resistance exhibits nonlinear behavior, which may originate from magnetic impurity scattering. These results highlight the crucial role of magnetic rare-earth Eu2+ ions in producing the exotic physical properties of the infinite-layer nickelates.
summary: The study reports on synthesizing and characterizing superconducting $	ext{Nd}_{1-x}	ext{Eu}_x	ext{NiO}_2$ thin films using PLD. Key findings include establishing a wide superconducting dome with high $T_c$ values and demonstrating field-enhanced superconductivity in both underdoped and overdoped regions. This work provides crucial experimental evidence regarding the role of magnetic rare-earth ions in these exotic correlated superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates the superconducting dome formation, field-enhanced superconductivity, and re-entrant behavior in infinite-layer nickelates ($	ext{Nd}_{1-x}	ext{Eu}_x	ext{NiO}_2$).
main_result: PLD synthesis successfully produced high-quality films exhibiting a wide superconducting dome with an optimal $T_c \approx 31$ K, and the system displays robust field enhancement in both underdoped and overdoped regimes.
method: The research employed Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) for film synthesis, followed by electrical transport measurements including resistivity ($ho(T)$), Hall effect ($R_H$), and upper critical field ($\mu_0 H_{c2}$).
model_or_system: The physical system is the infinite-layer nickelate $	ext{Nd}_{1-x}	ext{Eu}_x	ext{NiO}_2$ thin film, where superconductivity is modulated by Eu doping ($x$). The properties are linked to the magnetic rare-earth Eu$^{2+}$ ions.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), superconducting dome width (doping dependence), field enhancement magnitude, and nonlinear Hall resistance ($\Delta R_{xy}$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration $x$ ($0.2 \le x \le 0.5$), magnetic field strength (up to 35.6 T), and temperature range.
main_assumptions: The observed field enhancement suggests mechanisms beyond the simple Jaccarino-Peter effect, and nonlinear Hall response is attributed to magnetic impurity scattering.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate XRD confirming lattice changes with doping, $ho(T)$ showing superconducting transitions across the dome, and magnetotransport data detailing $H_{c2}$ kinks and re-entrant behavior in various doping regimes.
paper_structure: The paper details synthesis via PLD/reduction, presents transport measurements ($ho$, Hall), analyzes the doping dependence of $T_c$ (the superconducting dome), and investigates field effects to characterize the underlying pairing mechanism.
why_interesting: This work explores unconventional superconductivity in nickelates, a class of materials highly relevant to strongly correlated electron physics, which often shares theoretical links with high-Tc cuprates studied in AMO/condensed matter theory.
